title: The screenshot
hook: Your 1 a.m. rant just landed in the hostel group.

n1.text:
Last week, at 1 a.m., you vented to Tanvi about your roommate. The mugs, the alarms, all of it. This afternoon the Wing C group lights up. Tanvi has posted a screenshot of your chat.
Tanvi: lol she is SO done 😂
Seen by 14. Your roommate Ishita hasn't reacted yet.

choices.label: Reply in the group: "wow. thanks, Tanvi."
choices.consequence: The group goes silent. Two laughing emojis appear. Tanvi DMs you: "omg chill, it was funny". Now everyone is watching a fight.
choices.expert_note: Calling it out in public feels fair, and it is your right. It often turns the story into the fight, though, instead of what she did.

choices.label: DM Tanvi: "Please delete that. I told you that privately."
choices.consequence: She deletes it in two minutes. "sorry sorry, didn't think". Fourteen people still saw it.
choices.expert_note: Direct, private and specific. You said what you need without an audience. Deleting can't unsend it, but it stops it spreading.

choices.label: Say nothing and mute the group
choices.consequence: The screenshot stays up. By dinner Ishita is polite and cold. You don't know who has seen what.
choices.expert_note: Freezing is one of the most common reactions there is. It isn't a failure. Silence just leaves other people to decide what it all meant.

n2.text:
That evening your phone buzzes.
Tanvi: are you actually mad? it wasn't even that bad. everyone screenshots.

choices.label: "It's fine, forget it."
choices.consequence: She sends a heart. The awkwardness ends. You notice you now think twice before texting her anything real.
choices.expert_note: "It's fine" ends the awkward moment and keeps the problem. Trust usually shrinks quietly, like this.

choices.label: "It's not about how bad it was. I said it to you, not to 14 people."
choices.consequence:
Three dots for a long time.
Tanvi: ok. that's fair. i didn't think of it like that.
choices.expert_note: You named the real issue: permission, not content. That gives her something to understand instead of something to defend.

choices.label: "Would you be okay if I posted your chats?"
choices.consequence:
Tanvi: that's different
A minute later.
Tanvi: ok maybe not
choices.expert_note: Turning it around can land. It can also start a scoreboard. It works best as an honest question, not a gotcha.

n3.text: You get back to the room. Ishita is on her bed with her laptop. She has definitely seen it.

choices.label: "I should have said it to you, not about you. I'm sorry."
choices.consequence:
Ishita doesn't look up for a while.
Ishita: Yeah. You should have.
A long silence.
Ishita: The mug thing. I'll stop.
choices.expert_note: Two things happened here and you owned yours. That doesn't make what Tanvi did okay. Both can be true.

choices.label: "Tanvi shouldn't have shared that."
choices.consequence:
Ishita: But you still said it.
She goes back to her laptop.
choices.expert_note: You're right that sharing it was wrong. From where Ishita sits, the words hurt whoever showed them to her.

choices.label: Act normal. Ask if she wants chai.
choices.consequence:
Ishita: I'm good.
You both scroll your phones a metre apart.
choices.expert_note: Acting normal is a way to get through the evening. It leaves both of you guessing what the other is thinking.

end_a.title: Messy, but talking
end_a.text: It isn't fixed. But you two are talking in the room instead of about each other in chats. The next time Tanvi wants to forward something of yours, she asks first, half joking.
end_a.takeaway: What you say in private stays private unless you say otherwise. Sharing needs permission.

end_b.title: Two true things
end_b.text: Tanvi broke your trust, and your words hurt Ishita. Dinner is quiet. By the end of the week it still isn't resolved.
end_b.takeaway: Someone sharing your words without asking is on them, even when the rest of the situation is messy.

end_c.title: Nobody mentions it
end_c.text: The group moves on to memes. Ishita stays polite. You've stopped venting to Tanvi, and you miss it.
end_c.takeaway: When nobody names it, nobody learns that a screenshot needed a yes first.
